description: Global GameReel atom dictionary. Contains all mapped v4 atoms plus curated v5 idea-space atoms.

twist: all abilities come from items
base can be lost permanently
base is also the main vehicle
best reward requires making situation less safe
boss is an environmental system rather than creature
building rearranges during play
camera is a game mechanic
city itself is a moving machine
correct solution is often slower than risky shortcut
crafting happens by assembling real pieces
danger follows valuable resources
darkness changes level readability
death advances the story
debt replaces traditional experience points
dialogue happens during active gameplay
enemies are also useful resources
enemies learn player habits
enemy cannot be killed but can be redirected
entire game happens on a moving train
every enemy has one unique rule
every tool is also a weapon
every weapon is also a tool
everything valuable must be physically carried
factory is also the labyrinth
failure creates new opportunities
final objective is simply getting home
game begins after the apocalypse is already old
game deliberately breaks its own interface
inventory is physically represented in the world
inventory opens as physical object
large rooms are local mazes themselves
level is one giant machine
light is a limited resource
loot can invalidate completed objectives
main objective can be dismantled for parts
management decisions happen while action continues
map changes because of player systems
map has no minimap but uses strong landmarks
money is hidden until the end of the run
no permanent character upgrades
no teleport between exterior and interior
not every mystery has a reward
nothing is automatically extracted
one object is the center of the whole game
one player controls logistics while others act physically
one player has different information from others
only the base progresses
only the world progresses
optional work can be more valuable than mission objective
ordinary job becomes dangerous
player can finish task using parts stolen from optional systems
player chooses when to wake the facility
player inherits previous crews mistakes
player manages a place but performs all work manually
player repairs the world instead of conquering it
player works for an organization they never see
players can intentionally cause disasters for profit
players can split but communication becomes harder
players create most of the disasters themselves
players decide when run is over
players draw their own map
players see different versions of reality
powering lights also powers threats
previous failed runs leave physical traces
progress comes only from knowledge
progress resets but knowledge remains
quests are generated from current world state
resources are other machines/components
restoring infrastructure opens new hazards
roles are defined only by equipment
routes change after accidents
safe area slowly disappears
safe-looking rooms can become dangerous after blackout
secondary exits can emerge far from the vehicle
shop remains open during disasters
some dead ends contain absolutely nothing
sound is the primary navigation tool
team can leave at almost any time
temporary repair may fail later
the UI exists physically in the world
the environment is the enemy
the game takes place during one long shift
the map is physically continuous from base to dungeon
the safest route gives the smallest reward
time never pauses even in menus
time only advances when player acts
turning systems on makes map more dangerous
two gameplay loops feed each other
vehicle is the extraction boundary
victory increases future obligations
whole campaign happens in one evolving location
world generation uses real functional dependencies
world has no traditional enemies
world moves while player stays put
world reacts to noise physically
you can steal parts from working systems
you know the goal but not the exact reward

note: Internal v4 category visual is normalized to public reel id graphics in this master dictionary.
